title: Attacker abuses LearnWorlds free trials to send about 13,000 fake YouTube copyright phishing emails
date_note: Publication date; the campaign ran November 7 to 14.
geo_basis: headquarters (assumed, not stated in the article)
summary: The Register reports an attacker used automated tools to open about 570 free LearnWorlds trial accounts and rewrote the welcome email into fake YouTube copyright notices, about 13,000 in total, linking to a fake page showing a real Google OAuth consent screen. LearnWorlds says it found no unauthorised access to customer schools or personal data, removed the trial accounts and a paid account, and tightened bot checks.
plain: A scammer used an online course platform to send thousands of fake YouTube copyright warnings that tried to trick people into granting access to their Google accounts.
exec: Trusted SaaS email can be abused to deliver phishing that passes sender checks.
action: Do not click copyright notices; if you signed in on the fake page, change your Google password and review recent security activity and connected apps.

validation.note: One publisher read (The Register); LearnWorlds statement as reported there. Pin placed at the company's assumed headquarters.
